claims.text: [api axis, proposed] createContext<T>(key, default?) where default is a literal value or a factory `() => T`. No default: a read without a provider throws, as today. A factory default is not called at module scope: the first read without a provider in a page calls it and keeps the result as a provided value on that page's root scope (per request on the server, per page in the browser), so nothing lives in module scope and no CONTEXT_ADDED hook or madeContexts map is needed. A literal default is stored on the Context object and must be immutable (checked by the compiler, new BRM code). A non-factory object or store(...) default is a compile error.

evidence.detail: Vue builds a fresh default per read for factories; Solid keeps value defaults and advises primitives only. Neither stores the factory result per request root; that part is new here.

claims.text: Server and client fallback is one branch in the existing read: no provider found, then `context.d` literal or `root.v[key] ??= context.f()`, else throw missingContext. Because the factory result sits in root scope `v` like a provided value, the page state already serialises it and the client finds it with findProvider, so waitingReads, madeContexts and CONTEXT_ADDED (J4) are not restored. $hasContext(C) is true for a context with a default. Cost target: at most the 241 B gz that ui-no-defaults added in reverse, with the 32 B back from ui-store-guards, so under 250 B gz on the ui example.

claims.text: [api axis, proposed] $store(Ctx) stays as sugar: the analyzer rewrites `$store(Ctx)` to the key form it already emits for `$store($getContext(Ctx))`, so there is one runtime path and the signature is `$store<T>(source: StoreLike<T> | Context<StoreLike<T>>): T`, a superset of silmaril's `$store(store)`. With P1 a context that has a factory default needs no `$hasContext ? … : undefined` guard, so the 66 guarded $store(C) readers become plain `$store(C)` for contexts with a default, and stay guarded for the rest. Nullish sources stay an error (J9 ruling kept).

claims.text: A factory store written to root.v has no owner. Only stores made by $toStore in a provider carry [scope, site, slot] (shared.ts s(), server.ts toStore 747-751); the browser relinks them from that owner through madeStores/linkMadeStores. A factory result has no compiler site, so P2's 'the page state already serialises it' needs a new site allocator for factories, which P2 does not count. The client also cannot find the factory when no server read happened (a client-only first read): context.f lives in the context's module, which is the waitingReads/CONTEXT_ADDED problem of J4 again, since resume only loads a module when a scope needs it.

evidence.detail: Stores cross the page only through owner [scope, site, slot]; defaults had to be linked by module run (J4).

claims.ruling_why: J11: a value-only store crosses without an owner or site, and a browser-rendered reader imports the context it reads, so no site allocator or waitingReads is needed for a store nobody writes

claims.text: 'First read without a provider writes root.v' depends on read order and on streaming. The server writes provider values into the provider's record (record.v, server.ts:739-740). A first default read inside a streamed #loading chunk would write the root record after the root record went out in the first chunk, so the browser has no value and must run the factory itself, giving a second store that differs from the server's. P2 and P3 give no test or design for this. $hasContext 'static, fixed when the scope is made' (client/context.ts doc) also stops being true: true for a defaulted context before any write, and the value appears later.

claims.text: P3 turns 49 constant store(null) defaults into per-request stores. claims.text: Question 1, the only default still worth its cost: literal defaults only (P6, no factory). The default lives on the Context object, which the browser already imports (J11), so nothing is written to a record, nothing is serialised and no order problem exists (answers O2); no allocation per request (answers O3); an immutable literal cannot leak across requests (axis safety). It is Solid 2.0's own advice (primitives only, J5). But I measured the benefit as small: the number of ui contexts whose old default was a bare null, false or true and that are read with a guard is under 10 by a rough count (my regex may miss some), out of 140 guarded reads. On that count a literal default does not pay for 4 fallback sites and a new BRM code, and P7 plus P11 (O7) is the better value.
